answer: A strong defence is to make each identity pay a real, ongoing cost: stake a deposit that is slashed on fraud, like layers of shale that only form under pressure. Reputation should accrue slowly, the way a sonnet earns its shape line by line, so a fresh sybil starts with no standing. Every claim must be anchored to a basalt-hard proof — a verifiable credential or on-chain attestation that cannot be duplicated cheaply — so creating ten thousand fake agents costs ten thousand times as much as one honest one.
